verdict.reason: The finding is accurate as described. Table-cell background clearing is genuinely implemented in this tree: `normalizeCellStyleClears` is defined and exported (packages/docs/src/model/types.ts:269,307; index.ts:44; node.ts:74) and wired into both store cell paths (packages/docs/src/store/memory.ts:287 and packages/frontend/src/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.ts:2437), with dedicated tests. That is precisely the path the task doc excludes: the Non-goal names `applyTableCellStyle`, which routes into `doc.applyCellStyle` (packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts:3413-3434) and is invoked with `backgroundColor: ""` at packages/frontend/src/app/docs/docs-table-context-menu.tsx:233. Meanwhile docs/tasks/active/20260817-docs-highlight-none-clear-todo.md:44 still lists it as a Non-goal and the checklist (lines 30-39) never mentions the cell path or the cell helper, while docs/design/docs/docs-font-controls.md:246-259 now states the contract covers "table-cell background" and tables `normalizeCellStyleClears` against both cell stores. So the scope reversal is real and the two documents directly contradict each other. No guard makes this unreachable, and spec-conformance / scope-vs-stated-Non-goal / design-doc discipline is exactly this lens's lane, which rubric-classes an exceeded stated Non-goal as major.

This is the canonical doc the finding itself identifies, it is linked from docs/design/README.md:53, and it sits inside the L210-290 range the reviewer says they read, so no parallel/duplicate doc was created and CONTRIBUTING's update-the-existing-doc expectation is satisfied.
